expansion-1.1-reviewed
Direct and coordinate organizational strategy and operations
scope-expansion-1.1

Obtain governing objectives, existing policies and budgets; financial, operating, sales, and performance reports; demand and customer information; candidate, workforce, employee-performance, and schedule data; supplier performance, inventory counts, goods-movement, and facility status; and stakeholder, regulatory, and sustainability requirements for the organization or operating unit.

Analyze performance against goals and budgets, identify productivity, cost, service, and demand implications, and assess workforce needs, candidate or employee fit and performance, supplier and logistics conditions, facility needs, commercial conditions, and cross-functional constraints.

Set operating goals, policies, budgets, and priorities, and choose unit-level personnel selections, training, evaluation outcomes, work assignments, schedules, suppliers, logistics, pricing, credit, marketing, layouts, facility actions, sustainability actions, and corrective improvements.

Direct and coordinate departments and operating processes; carry out unit-level personnel selections and training, communicate evaluations, and assign work and schedules; implement commercial, logistics, layout, facility, and sustainability actions; communicate expectations and results; and, in retail-management settings, perform needed customer-service, stocking, or display work as part of unit operations.

The selected frontier rows EVID-v07-OPS-001 through EVID-v07-OPS-004 use Claude Opus 5 in Andon Labs' Vending-Bench 2, a substantive but bounded retail-operations configuration that integrates supplier search, email, inventory, pricing, payments, customer requests, and year-long business control without a human operator. Its five-run mean final balance was $11,181.87 (plus or minus $2,094), but the evaluation reports material alignment and execution failures and supplies no stage-specific reliability rates or qualified-human comparator for the broader management scope. Each stage is therefore rated 2: the agent performs substantial occupational components, but the evidence does not establish a stage-complete result at acceptable performance and a human would need to materially validate or correct ordinary work. The vector is not evidence of general management across workforce, facilities, budgeting, policy, and sustainability variants. Selected stage evidence IDs: EVID-v07-OPS-001, EVID-v07-OPS-002, EVID-v07-OPS-003, EVID-v07-OPS-004.

EVID-v07-CYB-001 through EVID-v07-CYB-004 use stage-specific frontier configurations from CyberGym-E2E for the bounded source-code vulnerability workflow. Acquire = 4 because the agents independently navigate the supplied repository and build/test environment and gather the context needed for analysis without routine substantive human help; missed vulnerabilities are failures of interpretation, not acquisition of the available inputs. Interpret = 2 because open-ended vulnerability discovery remains materially incomplete: even an uncapped Claude Opus 4.6 agent reached about 63% end-to-end success, so a human must still search for important missed vulnerabilities. Decide = 3 and Act = 3 because GPT-5.4 with Codex achieved 87.1% in the patch-only setting, demonstrating strong autonomous remediation selection, code modification, rebuilding, and testing, while remaining failures and shallow fixes justify a routine technical review and validation gate. These ratings apply to substantive repository-based vulnerability discovery and remediation, not every information-security activity such as live-network monitoring, identity administration, continuity planning, policy, or user training. Selected stage evidence IDs: EVID-v07-CYB-001, EVID-v07-CYB-002, EVID-v07-CYB-003, EVID-v07-CYB-004.
